> [!NOTE]
> This report was written by Claude (Anthropic's Claude Code) under the direction of @lukebakken, who reviewed it before filing. The analysis, the proposed fix and its tests were produced by Claude and verified against `main` before submission.

## Affected product

`amqp10_client`, the Erlang AMQP 1.0 client library published on Hex.pm and vendored in `rabbitmq-server` as `deps/amqp10_client`.

## Summary

`amqp10_client_connection:format_status/1` is the `gen_statem` status redactor: OTP calls it before the process state is written to a crash dump, and it also runs on `sys:get_status`. It delegates to `obfuscate_state_config_sasl/1`, whose only redacting clause matches `{plain, User, Pwd}`.

The connection state never holds that shape. `open/1` runs the config through `maybe_encrypt_sasl/1`, which converts `{plain, User, Pwd}` into `credentials_obfuscation:encrypt(term_to_binary(Plain))`, so `#state.config` holds an `encrypted_sasl()` — `{plaintext, Bin}` or `{encrypted, Bin}`. The decrypted tuple exists only in transient locals during the handshake. The redacting clause is therefore unreachable and the `Other -> Other` fallback returns the credential-bearing term unchanged.

`credentials_obfuscation:encrypt/1` returns `{plaintext, Bin}` whenever no obfuscation secret is configured, and no secret is configured by default. In that mode the stored value is `{plaintext, term_to_binary({plain, User, Pwd})}`, and the password is recoverable from it by inspection.

## Relationship to CVE-2026-67406

This is not that issue, and not a duplicate of it, but they are the same defect class and a reader will reasonably ask.

CVE-2026-67406 (GHSA-q44f-9vc5-grh7, patched 4.3.3 / 4.2.9 / 4.1.14 / 4.0.23) reported that the shovel `gen_server` processes implemented no `format_status` callback at all, so the crash reporter wrote their deobfuscated plaintext URIs to the error log. Its own text notes that `grep -rn format_status` across the shovel source returned zero results. The fix, a7cc6b5b50, added `format_status/1` to `rabbit_shovel_worker`.

That commit did not touch `amqp10_client_connection`, and the module's history since is unrelated to redaction. An AMQP 1.0 shovel starts an `amqp10_client_connection` process holding the same credentials, in the same supervision tree, and that process's redactor has been ineffective since 2023 — predating CVE-2026-67406 by two years. So the shovel worker is now redacted while its client connection is not.

The two differ in substance as well as in scope: CVE-2026-67406 concerned a missing callback exposing plaintext URIs, this concerns a present callback matching a shape the state never holds. They also affect different packages — that one `rabbitmq-server`, this one the `amqp10_client` Hex.pm package, which has consumers well beyond RabbitMQ.

## Impact depends on how the library is used

**Standalone users of `amqp10_client` are the affected population.** Nothing in the library sets an obfuscation secret, so the default is `{plaintext, ...}` and a crash dump or a captured `sys:get_status` carries the broker password in recoverable form.

**RabbitMQ brokers are materially less exposed, and less so than CVE-2026-67406 was.** `rabbit_prelaunch_dist:set_credentials_obfuscation_secret/0` always calls `credentials_obfuscation:set_secret/1` with the Erlang cookie, and `enabled` defaults to `true`, so on a node the unredacted term is PBE ciphertext rather than a password. That is weaker than intended — anyone able to read a crash dump can often read the cookie beside it — but unlike CVE-2026-67406, which exposed deobfuscated plaintext URIs, it is not direct credential disclosure. Within the broker the path is reachable through `rabbitmq_shovel`, which builds an AMQP 1.0 connection config from a shovel URI via `amqp10_client:parse_uri/1` (`rabbit_amqp10_shovel.erl`), and through `rabbitmq_amqp_client`.

Reading the data requires access to the node's crash dump or an Erlang shell on it, so this is a defence-in-depth failure in a redactor rather than a remotely reachable flaw. The redactor exists precisely because that material is expected to be handled or shipped less carefully than live process memory.

## Affected code

`deps/amqp10_client/src/amqp10_client_connection.erl`:

```erlang
obfuscate_state_config_sasl(Cfg) ->
    Sasl0 = maps:get(sasl, Cfg, none),
    Sasl = case Sasl0 of
               {plain, Username, _Password} ->   %% never matches
                   {plain, Username, <<"[redacted]">>};
               Other ->
                   Other                          %% credential passes through
           end,
    Cfg#{sasl => Sasl}.
```

The sibling `obfuscate_state_config_tls_opts/1` in the same redactor correctly strips `password` from the TLS proplist, so this is per-branch drift rather than a deliberate scope decision.

## This is a regression, and the provenance is exact

- 23e7639ae3 (2023-10-23) added `format_status/1` and this redactor. At that commit `open/1` did not encrypt, so the stored value really was `{plain, User, Pwd}` — **the redactor was correct as written**.
- 2316579c40 (2023-10-24) integrated `credentials_obfuscation`, adding `encrypt_sasl/1` and the `encrypted_sasl()` type. It changed the stored shape and did not update the redactor.

The earliest release tag containing 2316579c40 is `v3.13.0`.

## Suggested remediation

Redact by allowlist rather than by enumeration, so that a future SASL representation is redacted rather than passed through:

```erlang
Sasl = case Sasl0 of
           none -> none;
           anon -> anon;
           external -> external;
           {plain, Username, _Password} ->
               {plain, Username, <<"[redacted]">>};
           {plaintext, _} ->
               {plaintext, <<"[redacted]">>};
           {encrypted, _} ->
               {encrypted, <<"[redacted]">>};
           _ ->
               {plaintext, <<"[redacted]">>}
       end,
```

Enumerating the two `encrypted_sasl()` shapes alone would fix the observed leak but preserve the failure mode that caused it: the denylist shape is what allowed an unrelated change to reintroduce the leak silently.

A commit implementing this, with two `eunit` cases, is ready to push to a private fork on request. The first asserts that the password does not appear anywhere in `term_to_binary/1` of the whole formatted status, rather than checking the `sasl` field, and asserts the password is recoverable *before* redaction so it cannot pass vacuously. Reverse-applying the fix makes it fail. `gmake dialyze` and `gmake xref` are unchanged against `main`.

## Steps to reproduce

Not runtime-confirmed against a live crash dump. Verified by source inspection on `main` and by unit test: with no obfuscation secret set, `maybe_encrypt_sasl({plain, User, Pwd})` returns `{plaintext, term_to_binary({plain, User, Pwd})}`, and `format_status/1` returns a state from which that term is recoverable verbatim.

## Credit

Found while reviewing static-analysis findings against the 4.3.6 source.
